name: Cornwall Alliance

summary.text: The Cornwall Alliance for the Stewardship of Creation, led by E. Calvin Beisner, is an evangelical group opposing climate-change policy; it released the 'Resisting the Green Dragon' video series in 2010. DeSmog reports it operates as a project of the James Partnership, which does not disclose its donors; more than half of the James Partnership's roughly $340,000 of 2012 income came from Donors Trust, and about a quarter of its income went to Beisner's salary. A 2010 report found Cornwall and CFACT shared the fundraising firm ClearWord Communications and that Beisner sat on CFACT's board.

sources.title: Cornwall Alliance for the Stewardship of Creation

facts.claim: DeSmog reports that the James Partnership, which runs the Cornwall Alliance as a project, chooses not to disclose its funding sources, and that per Conservative Transparency more than half of its $340,000 of 2012 income came from Donors Trust.
facts.quote: more than half of the James Partnership's $340,000 of income in 2012 came from the "dark money" funding group known as Donors Trust (DT)

sources.title: Cornwall Alliance for the Stewardship of Creation

facts.claim: A 2015 DeSmog background document says that, according to US tax records, about a quarter of the James Partnership's income is spent on the salary of Calvin Beisner, the Cornwall Alliance's founder and spokesperson.
facts.quote: about one quarter of the James Partnership's income is spent on the salary of Calvin Beisner

facts.claim: A 2010 ThinkProgress report (reposted) said Washington State filings showed CFACT and the Cornwall Alliance shared a common fundraising firm, ClearWord Communications Group, and that Beisner was a CFACT board member; Cornwall's spokesman denied any relationship with CFACT.
facts.quote: share a common fundraising firm, ClearWord Communications Group

facts.claim: DeSmog reports that CDR Communications, whose head also ran the James Partnership, produced the 'Resisting the Green Dragon' video series for the Cornwall Alliance.
facts.quote: including the "Resisting the Green Dragon" video series

openQuestions: Site claim (Cornwall leaders worked with fossil-funded groups CFACT and Heartland) is supported for CFACT by the 2010 report; the Heartland link appears only through Cornwall's listing as a 2009 Heartland conference sponsor in DeSmog's tally, which recorded no Exxon/Scaife/Koch funding for Cornwall itself. Cornwall's own 990s were not opened; all funding figures are from advocacy outlets and are labelled as reported.
